summary: All five Round 1 findings are resolved: the corpus scorer now requires exact flag decisions and forbids blocks, real job() tests exercise capped-block and silent-pass state, the fallback-bearing article is persisted and reused in the reverse arrival order, raw 0.30/0.50 boundaries and their immediate lower neighbors are classified, and malformed/non-dict/legacy fingerprints plus an absent candidate title are covered. The added result-handling failure test also proves that a failure after assigning the flag delay clears both the fingerprint and stale defer. Focused unit/corpus and integration suites pass. One minor current-task assertion is ineffective: the single-line diagnostic check inspects JSON serialization instead of the diagnostic fields. No pre-existing debt or adjacent improvement is raised by this scoped review.

findings.issue: Current-task defect: assert "\n" not in json.dumps(suppressed) cannot prove that diagnostic fields are single-line, because json.dumps escapes embedded newlines as the two characters \\n. The assertion passes even if a title or source_name still contains a literal newline; the surrounding secret-redaction and size assertions remain meaningful.
findings.recommendation: Assert directly over every emitted text field, for example that none of '\n', '\r', or any Unicode control-category character occurs in item['title'], item['source_name'], or item['link']. Keep the existing JSON-based secret checks and length bounds. This makes removal of the single-line normalization fail the test without changing production code or broadening scope.
